## Problem

Production deploy has been failing consistently (3 consecutive failures). All 34/42 admin integration E2E tests fail with `ADMIN_API_TOKEN is not configured on this Worker.`

## Root Cause

The auth middleware checks for `ADMIN_API_TOKEN` from `c.env`, but the production Cloudflare Worker has the admin token configured under the **legacy name** `ADMIN_TOKEN` (confirmed via `wrangler secret list`). The env var was renamed in code but the production secret was never updated.

## Fix

- Check `ADMIN_API_TOKEN` first (preferred/new name)
- Fall back to `ADMIN_TOKEN` (legacy name for backward compatibility)
- Updated `Env` interface to include `ADMIN_TOKEN` as optional

This is a backward-compatible change — existing production secret continues to work without requiring any new `wrangler secret put` commands.

## Verification

CI will run and the Deploy — Production workflow should pass its admin integration E2E tests after this is merged.
recent_prs.title: fix: fall back to legacy ADMIN_TOKEN env var when ADMIN_API_TOKEN is not set

recent_prs.body:
Adds a fire-and-forget OTel span for LLM call timing inside the AI Tutor's callLLM() function. This allows SigNoz to track LLM latency separately from HTTP request latency.

Span attributes:
- `tutor.llm.model` — model name
- `tutor.llm.status` — HTTP status or 'error'
- `tutor.llm.duration_ms` — LLM round-trip time

The existing global `instrumentRequest` (in the fetch handler) already captures HTTP-level spans for all routes including the AI Tutor. This adds sub-span visibility into the LLM call itself.

## What

Switches the Canvas PWA from a monolithic 971-line `pwa.js` to a modular ES module architecture (10 files, 1,235 lines total). Brings three new features from the FRS:

### New Features

| Feature | FRS Req | Implementation |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **Inline property editor** | R1 | Double-click any object title → inline edit field → auto-save to IndexedDB |
| **Undo/Redo** | R2 | Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, 50-level history stack, captures full object+proposal state |
| **Keyboard shortcuts** | R3 | Delete removes selected, Escape deselects all |

### Architecture

```
js/
├── main.js                 — entry point (imports + init)
├── canvas-state.js         — shared state, constants, DOM refs
├── canvas-interactions.js  — drag, resize, snap, pan, select (491 lines)
├── canvas-render.js        — render/paint objects
├── canvas-selection.js     — selection logic
├── canvas-proposals.js     — proposal system
├── canvas-persistence.js   — IndexedDB save/load
├── canvas-keyboard.js      — keyboard shortcuts
├── canvas-properties.js    — double-click inline editing
└── canvas-history.js       — undo/redo stack
```

### Files changed
- `apps/pwa-canvas/public/index.html` — switch from pwa.js to js/main.js module

## What

Delivers the remaining governance toolchain from the research sprint:
Saga coordinator, DAG scheduler, reconciliation loop, replay testing,
cross-mission memory, unified Aegis CLI, red-team testing, tamper-proof
audit, CI integration, and dogfood verification.

## Changes

### Governance Engine
- **Saga coordinator** (tools/saga.py): multi-step mission execution with
  auto-compensation on failure, checkpoint-based rollback, reconciliation
  loop after each task
- **DAG scheduler** (tools/scheduler.py): parallel task execution with
  cycle detection, dependency-gated fan-in, failure cascading
- **Replay testing** (tools/replay.py): replay past missions from audit
  history against current codebase
- **Cross-mission memory** (tools/mission_memory.py): SQLite-backed
  persistence of mission outcomes with recall by file path or mission ID

### Aegis CLI (tools/aegis.py)
Unified 5-phase state machine:
  DISCOVERY → validate manifest, score risks
  ALIGNMENT → build DAG, check dependencies
  GATE → authorization level check
  EXECUTION → Saga coordinator with reconcile
  VERIFICATION → store memory, produce audit report

Subcommands: run, replay, memory, risk-score, policy validate

### Security & Integrity
- **Tamper-proof audit** — each report includes previous_mission_hash
  + mission_hash (SHA-256), forming verifiable chain
- **Red-team tests** (tools/redteam_test.py) — 6 tests, all passing:
  forbidden path, missing compensate, missing saga, cycle detection,
  policy integrity, saga compensation
- **CI integration** — Aegis policy validate + red-team tests run on
  every push/PR
- **Risk taxonomy** — per-operation scoring (1-10), authorization level
  mapping (gogo vs deploy gogo)

### Fixes
- calculators.ts no longer imports deprecated compile-layout-compat
  (caused Vitest teardown race in CI)
- compile-layout-compat.ts doc cleaned up

## Verification
- [x] Full Aegis 5-phase pipeline run against real manifest (exit 0)
- [x] Red-team tests: 6/6 pass
- [x] Policy validation: 8/8 checks pass
- [x] Hash chain: reports link via previous_mission_hash
- [x] Memory: 9 mission records stored

## Problem

The Deploy — Production workflow runs `wrangler deploy --env production` but `wrangler.json` had no `env.production` section. Wrangler would:
- Deploy as `edgegde-calculator-production` (not the intended `edgegde-calculator`)
- Try to register top-level queue consumers on the new worker name, which failed because the queues already have `edgegde-calculator` as a consumer

## Fix

Added `env.production` section to `wrangler.json` with:
- `name: edgegde-calculator` — deploys as the correct worker name
- `queues.producers` only — keeps queue producer bindings available but does NOT register queue consumers (avoids conflict with the base worker's existing consumer registration)

Also deleted the stale `edgegde-calculator-production` worker from the failed deploy attempt.
